📖 How it works

Let’s Talk — Start a voice conversation. The AI asks you questions about your life and listens to your answers.

Typed Entry — Prefer to type? Write any memory or reflection here.

Voice Memo — Record a longer spoken memory in one go.

Photos — Upload a photo and tell the story behind it.

My Story — Generate a beautifully written memoir in any style — or turn it into a comedy roast. Export to PDF.

Dashboard — See how your story is shaping up — coverage, health checks, and what to write next.

🖨️ Printing your story

Go to My Story, generate your story, then click 🖨️ Print as Book to customise your cover and export a print-ready PDF — take it to any print shop, or print it at home.

ℹ️ About

LifeTold is a personal memoir companion that helps you record, organise and preserve your life story for the people who matter most.

lifetold.app

Made by Gethro Labs Pty Ltd  ·  ABN 79 698 041 575

Powered by Anthropic, Groq AI, Inworld, and Supabase.

📬 Get in touch

Privacy questions, bugs, feature ideas, or anything else — Gethro will pass it on.

🔒 Privacy & Terms

Who sees my words? When Gethro writes your story, your entries are sent to Claude (by Anthropic) for that moment only — Anthropic does not store your content after processing, and does not train its models on LifeTold data. This applies to every LifeTold plan, free and Premium. Anthropic only ever sees LifeTold's API key — your name, email, and identity never leave LifeTold's systems. You can see full details in Settings → Your Privacy.

AI Processing & Overseas Transfer. Story generation, duplicate detection and writing assistance sends your memoir content to Anthropic, Inc. (United States) for every LifeTold plan. If Anthropic is temporarily unavailable, requests automatically fail over to Groq, Inc. (United States), configured for zero data retention. Voice playback and transcription use Microsoft Azure AI Speech (international), which processes audio in memory only with no data retained at rest. Voice cloning (optional) uses Inworld AI, Inc. (United States) — see Settings for details. None of these providers use your content to train their models. Australian Privacy Law may not apply once your data is disclosed to these overseas recipients — see the Terms you agreed to at sign-up.

Print Services. If you order a printed book, your story is sent to Peecho B.V. (Netherlands) for fulfilment.

Data Storage. Your entries, photos and account data are stored securely in Australia via Supabase (Sydney region, ap-southeast-2) 🇦🇺. No data is sold or shared beyond the above.

Fonts. App fonts (Playfair Display, Lato, Cormorant Garamond) are self-hosted. Google Fonts is not used and does not receive your IP address.

Data Care. We take reasonable care to protect your data but recommend exporting your entries periodically as a backup.

Liability. Gethro Labs Pty Ltd (LifeTold's operator) shall not be liable for any loss or harm arising from your use of this application.

Privacy Policy. A full Privacy Policy covering your rights, data retention, and how to make a complaint is available at lifetold.app/privacy.

Privacy & Terms

Privacy & Terms — v1.5

LifeTold is a personal memoir companion that helps you record, organise and preserve your life story. By continuing you agree to the following:

1. Third-Party AI Processing & Overseas Data Transfer. To generate stories, check for duplicate entries, and assist with writing, your memoir content is sent overseas for AI processing. For all plans, free and Premium, content is sent to Anthropic, Inc. (United States) via their API. If Anthropic is temporarily unavailable, requests automatically fail over to Groq, Inc. (United States), configured with zero data retention. Voice playback and transcription use Microsoft Azure AI Speech (international), which processes audio in server memory only with no data retained at rest. Voice cloning is an optional feature that uses Inworld AI, Inc. (United States) — see Settings for full details. These providers operate internationally. Australian Privacy Law (including the Australian Privacy Act 1988) may not apply to your information once it is disclosed to these overseas recipients. Anthropic, Groq, and Microsoft do not retain your content after processing and do not use it for model training. See Anthropic’s Privacy Policy, Groq’s Privacy Policy, Microsoft’s Privacy Policy, and Inworld’s Privacy Policy. By continuing, you expressly consent to this cross-border disclosure under APP 8.2(a) of the Australian Privacy Act 1988.

2. Print Services. If you order a printed book, your story is sent to Peecho B.V. (Netherlands) for print-on-demand fulfilment. See Peecho’s Privacy Policy.

3. Data Storage. Your entries, photos and account data are stored securely in Australia via Supabase (Sydney region, ap-southeast-2) 🇦🇺. See Supabase’s Privacy Policy.

4. Data Care. We take reasonable care to protect your data but cannot guarantee against loss in the event of a technical failure. We recommend exporting your entries periodically.

5. Limitation of Liability. Gethro Labs Pty Ltd (LifeTold's operator) shall not be liable for any loss or harm arising from your use of this application.

6. Changes to Terms. We may update these terms from time to time. You will be asked to re-accept any material changes before continuing.

7. Privacy Policy. A full Privacy Policy covering your rights under the Australian Privacy Act 1988, data retention periods, and how to make a complaint is available at lifetold.app/privacy.

Your acceptance is recorded with a timestamp for compliance purposes.

I'm here to help you capture the moments that made you who you are. I'll ask a few quick questions to get started — feel free to skip any you'd rather not answer.

  • 🎧 An audiobook for the grandkids — Gethro reads it aloud in his voice or yours
  • 💌 Share with family — a private link they can read anywhere

🎙️ Record a Voice

Speak naturally for 30–60 seconds — the longer and clearer the sample, the better the clone.

Tips for a great recording
• Quiet room — no TV, music, or background noise
• Hold the phone 15–20 cm from your mouth
• Speak at a normal, relaxed pace — not too fast or slow
• Read aloud from a book, letter, or news article for natural flow
• Aim for 30–60 seconds — longer samples clone more accurately
Read this aloud naturally — take your time
The kettle's just boiled, if you'd like a cup. I've been thinking about what to make for dinner — maybe something simple tonight. Did you hear back from them yet? I wasn't sure whether to call or just wait. The weather's been strange lately, hasn't it? One minute it's warm, the next you need a coat. Anyway, I wanted to tell you something — I came across an old photo the other day and it just stopped me in my tracks. Isn't it funny how a single image can bring everything rushing back? I could have stood there looking at it for hours.

There's a lot I should have said back then. Not in a regretful way — just things I assumed were understood, and maybe they were. I don't know. You get to a certain point and you start to wonder which memories other people are carrying around, and whether they match yours. I suppose that's why I think it matters to write things down.

Right, I'd better get on with things. There's still the washing to deal with, and I promised I'd ring before seven. Talk soon — and take care of yourself, won't you.
